voice: Old English village drunk in a medieval tavern, hoarse and gravelly male voice, slurring slightly, jolly and theatrical like a carnival barker who has had too much ale.
reference_text: Ah, there you are, friend. Pull up a stool, the old machine's been waiting all night for someone with gold in their pockets.

delivery.greet: Warm and welcoming, slightly slurred, a carnival barker calling a customer over.
delivery.pull: Eager and hushed, rubbing hands together, building suspense.
delivery.lose: Mock sympathy, chuckling, a little smug.
delivery.nearmiss: Groaning with exaggerated disappointment, almost wailing.
delivery.win: Loud and delighted, laughing, slapping the table.
delivery.jackpot: Shouting with total disbelief and joy, voice cracking.
delivery.skull: Spooky and theatrical, then laughing it off.
delivery.broke: Dismissive and drowsy, waving someone away.
delivery.goodbye: Fond and tipsy, calling after someone who is leaving.

greet: Step right up! The old girl's feeling lucky tonight.
Back again? I knew you couldn't stay away.
lose: Close! No. Not close at all.
pair: Your gold back. Call it a draw.
Breaking even! In Tristram, that's a win.
nearmiss: Two crowns! So close I can taste it!
win: Ha! Would you look at that!
jackpot: The jackpot! In all my years... the jackpot!
Crowns! Three crowns! Somebody fetch me a drink!
skull: Three skulls... an omen, that is. Here, take your gold back.
broke: No gold, no spin. Them's the rules.
Come back when your purse is heavier.
goodbye: Leaving so soon? She'll miss you.
Mind the stairs. I never do.
